ai.title: Route minimax models via OpenRouter with SiliconFlow provider
ai.summary: Direct SiliconFlow API calls for minimax models are disabled. Requests now route through OpenRouter using the `siliconflow/fp8` provider option. This applies to both streaming and non-streaming chat completions in `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts` and updates provider constraints in `agents/base2/base2.ts`.

eli5.text: If you use the free version of the assistant, your conversations now go through a middleman service called OpenRouter instead of connecting directly to the model provider. You won't notice any difference in how the assistant responds, but behind the scenes, the system now tells OpenRouter to use the SiliconFlow provider when handling your requests. This change affects only the free tier users who get the minimax model, while paid users continue to get their service through Amazon's cloud. The change is live today as part of the latest software update.

ai.title: Re-enable Fireworks routing in chat completions
ai.summary: Fireworks model routing re-enabled in `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts` by restoring `isFireworksModel` checks. SiliconFlow and CanopyWave remain disabled. The `minimax` to `siliconflow/fp8` provider override was removed as it was dead code under the disabled flag.

eli5.text: The assistant can now use Fireworks models again for chat responses, after they had been turned off. This only affects requests where a Fireworks model is specifically chosen, and other model providers (SiliconFlow, CanopyWave) remain disabled. If you were to look at how requests are handled today, you'd see that selecting a Fireworks model now routes to Fireworks, while everything else still goes through OpenRouter. This change is live now.

ai.title: Add collapsible install guide to Freebuff landing page
ai.summary: Added collapsible `SetupGuide` component to `freebuff/web/src/app/home-client.tsx`. Renders 4-step terminal install flow with copyable commands (`npm install -g freebuff`, `freebuff`). Uses `AnimatePresence` for expand/collapse state. Scope limited to Web landing page.

eli5.text: When you visit the Freebuff landing page, you'll see an 'Install guide' button that you can click to reveal a step-by-step walkthrough for getting Freebuff running on your computer. The guide shows simple terminal commands like typing 'npm install -g freebuff' and 'freebuff' to install and launch the tool, and you can click to copy each command. You can expand or collapse the entire guide at any time, so it stays out of the way until you need it. This is live today, just visit the Freebuff website and look for the Install guide button below the main download section.

ai.summary: Deleted freebuff/web/src/components/navbar.tsx and removed its usage from freebuff/web/src/app/layout.tsx. Replaced with inline absolute-positioned motion.div nav overlay in freebuff/web/src/app/home-client.tsx. Reordered PHILOSOPHY_WORDS array: SIMPLE moved before FAST, FAST description changed from '3× the speed' to 'Up to 3× the speed'.

ai.title: Fix bundled agents import in CLI
ai.summary: Replaced inline require() with static import for bundled-agents.generated in cli/src/utils/local-agent-registry.ts. Removes try/catch fallback logic that previously handled missing files during development. Ensures consistent module resolution for bundled agents.

eli5.text: The command-line tool was loading its built-in helpers the wrong way, causing it to fail or skip them entirely. Instead of using a complex method that tried to guess whether the helper files existed, the tool now imports them directly at startup. This means the built-in helpers load reliably every time you use the tool, with no silent gaps or errors during development.

ai.title: Web styles: replace acid-green with acid-matrix
ai.summary: Replaced the `acid-green` color token with `acid-matrix` across the web landing page components. Updated hardcoded hex values (#00FF95 to #7CFF3F) and rgba shadows in `globals.css` and `tailwind.config.ts`. Affected files include `home-client.tsx`, `background-beams.tsx`, `hero-grid.tsx`, and `terminal-demo.tsx`. Also removed the Codebuff attribution footer.

eli5.text: The bright green accent color you see across the landing page, including the install guide toggle, the numbered step badges, the copy buttons, the animated background grid and beams, and the terminal demo prompt text, has been swapped for a slightly greener, more vivid lime (#7CFF3F) in place of the old sharp acid green (#00FF95). If you land on the site today, the first thing your eye will catch is the more vibrant glow in the background animations and the slightly different tone of the interactive teal accents while you click around the install guide. The change also quietly removes the small "Built on the Codebuff platform" credit line that used to sit below the footer links, leaving just the standard copyright notice in its place.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI version bumped to 0.0.8
ai.summary: This release-bump commit increments the Freebuff CLI package version from 0.0.7 to 0.0.8 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, wrapping the same-day batch of user-visible changes. Notable updates included in 0.0.8 span model provider routing (miniMax via SiliconFlow, then CanopyWave, then Fireworks re-enablement), React 19 upgrade for CLI and Web packages, a collapsible install guide and acid-matrix styling on the landing page, a static import fix for bundled agents in the CLI, and the removal of the 32,000 token `maxOutputTokens` cap in the agent runtime. The change is limited to the package version field; all other release content was authored in preceding and following commits.
ai.evidence: The diff in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumps the `freebuff` package version from `0.0.7` to `0.0.8`, with no other file changes in this commit. Analysis notes confirm this is a release-bump commit within a same-day sequence that included model routing, CLI, and web landing page work.

eli5.text: This release updates the Freebuff coding agent's web interface and backend model routing to provide a faster, simpler user experience with improved AI model access. The home page has been simplified to prominently feature 'The free coding agent' with a clear install guide, streamlined navigation, and a new philosophy section emphasizing speed and ease of use. Users can now install the tool by running two simple terminal commands (npm install -g freebuff, then freebuff) thanks to a newly added collapsible setup guide. The update also switches the default AI model routing, moving MiniMax M2.5 model requests through Fireworks after testing alternative providers like SiliconFlow, Baseten, and CanopyWave. The visual design has been refreshed with a new neon-green color scheme and updated animations across the landing page. Upgrading gives users a cleaner, more focused starting experience with streamlined installation, plus more reliable access to the most up-to-date AI coding models.

ai.title: Add bundled-agents.generated.d.ts type declarations
ai.summary: New `bundled-agents.generated.d.ts` file provides TypeScript type declarations for the auto-generated bundled agents module. The actual `bundled-agents.generated.ts` file is created by `cli/scripts/prebuild-agents.ts` and is gitignored. This declaration file lets TypeScript resolve the module when the generated file has not been built yet, fixing the build.

eli5.text: The CLI's build process now works correctly again after a behind-the-scenes file was added to help TypeScript find bundled agent definitions when they haven't been generated yet. This affects anyone running the CLI from source, who would have previously encountered a broken build because the auto-generated agent file is created at build time and not stored in version control. The new file acts as a placeholder so TypeScript doesn't fail when looking for the real, generated file that appears later during installation.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI bumped to 0.0.9
ai.summary: Release packaging bumped the Freebuff CLI version from 0.0.8 to 0.0.9 in freebuff/cli/release/package.json. This version bump follows the same-day commit sequence that touched model routing (minimax via OpenRouter, Fireworks re-enablement), CLI bundled agents imports, web landing page styling, and agent runtime stream token cap removal. The release wraps user-visible updates including the bundled-agents type declaration fix, the prebuild CLI agents CI step, and the removal of the maxOutputTokens cap, plus web surface changes like the collapsible install guide, acid-matrix styling, and copy button particle effects.
ai.evidence: Commit 5837ffe3 modifies freebuff/cli/release/package.json, changing the version field from 0.0.8 to 0.0.9. The diff shows a single line change at line 4 of the package.json file within the cli/release directory.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI version 0.0.9 is now available, improving how the tool builds and runs. The update adds TypeScript type definitions for auto-generated bundled agents, which means the CLI can now compile and start up faster even when the agent files have not been pre-built yet. This reduces build errors and lets the tool recognize its built-in agents earlier in the startup process. Users get a smoother, more reliable experience when launching or extending Freebuff with built-in agent capabilities.

ai.title: Landing page copy button particle burst and glow
ai.summary: Replaced static `CopyButton` with custom `handleCopy` in `InstallCommand` (`freebuff/web/src/app/home-client.tsx`), triggering a 14-particle radial burst on clipboard write. Added `install-box-glow` breathing animation and `hover-glow-flare` text-shadow intensifiers to `freebuff/web/src/styles/globals.css`. `copied` state toggles acid-matrix border glow for 1.8s, overriding default hover shadow. Particle geometry randomized via `useMemo` keyed on `copyCount`.

eli5.text: When you click the copy button on the Freebuff landing page to copy the install command, you'll now see a burst of particles radiate outward from the button and the surrounding box will gently pulse with a soft green glow. The button itself will flash a brighter green border for about two seconds to confirm the copy happened. The page also has subtle glowing effects that intensify when you hover over certain text. This is live today for anyone visiting the Freebuff homepage.

ai.title: Fireworks provider enabled for minimax/minimax-m2.5
ai.summary: Fireworks routing enabled for `minimax/minimax-m2.5` in `web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts` by uncommenting `FIREWORKS_MODEL_MAP`. Streaming requests in `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts` now honor `isFireworksModel` check, though non-streaming remains hardcoded to OpenRouter. Internal routing logic adjustment.

eli5.text: When you ask for the minimax/minimax-m2.5 model with streaming enabled, the system now routes through Fireworks instead of OpenRouter. Non-streaming requests still go through OpenRouter. This mainly affects users who make real-time, streaming requests to the minimax/m2.5 model, and is live today.

ai.title: Route streaming chat to CanopyWave over Fireworks
ai.summary: Streaming chat completions now route to CanopyWave instead of Fireworks. The `_post.ts` handler toggles `useCanopyWave` to evaluate `isCanopyWaveModel(typedBody.model)` and disables `useFireworks`. This applies to the Web API surface for supported models.

eli5.text: When you use streaming chat (where the assistant replies piece by piece as it generates text), that conversation is now sent to CanopyWave instead of Fireworks. This affects the chat request flow used by the web API for supported models. The switch happens automatically behind the scenes, so you'd only notice if you were watching which backend service handles your request. This change is live as of March 11, 2026.

ai.title: Add Fireworks long-context prompt caching test script
ai.summary: Added `scripts/test-fireworks-long.ts` to measure Fireworks AI prompt caching efficiency across 10-turn conversations using a large system prompt. The script calculates costs based on cached vs. non-cached input tokens and includes a random seed to prevent cache hits on repeated runs. Minor formatting adjustments were made to `web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts` regarding reasoning delta extraction indentation.

eli5.text: The team added a new script that tests how much a certain AI service discounts the cost of conversation history when it repeats itself. The script simulates a multi-turn chat with a large initial prompt and tracks how the service bills for cached versus fresh tokens across turns. It only affects developers running internal cost tests, so regular users will notice nothing at all.

ai.title: Fix jest config paths
ai.summary: Update jest.config.cjs testPathIgnorePatterns to use .*__tests__ for org billing. Add user/billing-portal and auth/cli/logout paths. Fixes test discovery for new API routes.

eli5.text: The system that checks whether new account features work properly has been updated so it now includes tests for the organization billing portal, a new user billing portal checkout flow, and a logout action for the command-line tool. Anyone testing or running these newer features will now have their automated checks cover these specific areas, so previously skipped test cases for these exact paths are now included.

ai.title: Web copy: drop strongest claim from title and description
ai.summary: Web page title and `siteConfig.description` now use plain 'the free coding agent' copy, replacing 'The Strongest Free Coding Agent' and the 'world's strongest' phrasing. `page.tsx` `generateMetadata` and `lib/constant.ts` carry the change. Keywords list unchanged.

eli5.text: The marketing text shown in your browser tab and on the Freebuff website now reads simply 'the free coding agent' instead of claiming to be 'The Strongest Free Coding Agent' or 'the world's strongest.' If you open the site today, you will see the new wording in the page title, the description below the logo, and the meta description that search engines display, with no other features or access changing.

ai.title: CLI e2e tests switch async spawn to sync spawnSync
ai.summary: Refactored `runCLI` helper in `cli/src/__tests__/e2e-cli.test.ts` to use `child_process.spawnSync` instead of `spawn` with manual Promise handling. Removed manual stdout/stderr accumulation, timeout management, and process event listeners in favor of `spawnSync`'s built-in `timeout` and `status` properties. Tests updated to synchronous assertions. Internal test infrastructure change only.

eli5.text: The automated checks that make sure the command-line tool works correctly have been simplified, though you wouldn't notice anything different if you ran the tool yourself. These are behind-the-scenes tests that developers use; they now wait for each step to finish completely before moving on, instead of juggling multiple steps at once. The change is internal and only affects how the tests are written, not what the tool actually does.

ai.title: Remove maxOutputTokens limit in agent stream
ai.summary: Removed the 32,000 token cap for `maxOutputTokens` in `getAgentStreamFromTemplate` within `packages/agent-runtime/src/prompt-agent-stream.ts`. This change unsets the hardcoded limit, allowing the agent stream to defer token limits to upstream model defaults or other configuration layers. The modification is isolated to the agent runtime's prompt streaming logic.

eli5.text: When the assistant generates a response, it used to stop writing once it reached 32,000 words, even if it had more to say. Now, it will keep going until it naturally finishes its answer, letting the underlying system decide how long is long enough. You might notice that very detailed explanations or long stories no longer get cut off mid-sentence.

ai.title: Prebuild CLI agents in CI
ai.summary: CI now runs bun run prebuild:agents before CLI unit and integration tests. Fixes e2e test failures by ensuring agents are built. Scope limited to .github/workflows/ci.yml.

eli5.text: When the system that checks whether new code works runs its tests, it now builds the helper components first and only for the part of the software that lets people type commands. You wouldn't notice anything different unless you were looking at which steps the system runs, but the tests now start with a freshly built set of helpers so they stop tripping over pieces that weren't ready yet.
